text:
amal: Heads-up — ran into a confusing import behaviour across Node ESM, CJS, and Edge runtimes. Docs show both `require('@redwood/inference')` and `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` but examples aren't consistent.
amal: In a Node CJS project `require`ing the package returns an object so `const client = new (require('@redwood/inference'))()` blows up with `TypeError: require(...) is not a constructor`.
amal: Example snippet that surprised me:
```js
// CommonJS
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
```
amal: That fails for me. With `esModuleInterop` turned off the shape is `{ default: [Function] }` so you need `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference').default` which is awkward.
jeremy: ^ yep we saw that too. Edge runtimes (Cloudflare/Vercel) force ESM and some bundlers tree-shake differently. The package currently ships both CJS and ESM entry points but our docs don't make it clear which path you hit.
tara: Can you paste the exact error from an Edge deploy? we might need to update the `exports` field in package.json or add a dedicated `edge` entrypoint.
amal: On Vercel Edge I got `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` when using CJS example. When using `import` I get `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor` — so confusing.
mike: For TS users there's also typing friction: without `esModuleInterop` your `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` might not match the `export =` shape. We should document three canonical patterns: Node CJS, Node ESM, Edge/Workers.
tara: Agreed. Proposal for docs:
- Node (CommonJS): `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference')` or `const RedwoodClient = require('@redwood/inference').default` if you prefer default style and enable `esModuleInterop`.
- Node (ESM): `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` or `import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference'` depending on `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`/`esModuleInterop`.
- Edge (ESM-only runtimes): prefer ESM named imports and a dedicated `@redwood/inference/edge` entry if necessary.
jeremy: Also add a short snippet for tsconfig settings:
```json
// tsconfig.json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true,
    "module": "ESNext"
  }
}
```
jeremy: And a runtime checklist: bundler target, `type` in package.json, and which `exports` entry is used.
amal: Would also be great to include short repros for common errors users paste in support. Lots of threads where users paste the `is not a constructor` error and we end up asking for their bundler config.
tara: I'll open a docs PR with three minimal examples + note about `exports` and TS flags. @mike can you add a short Edge-specific code sample (Cloudflare Worker + fetch) so it's explicit?
mike: Yep, I'll add a Cloudflare Worker example and a Vercel Edge function snippet. Also add suggestion to check `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/inference')"` to see which file is being loaded locally.
dev-bot: PR created: docs/sdk-import-matrix — reviewers: @tara, @jeremy (link: https://git.redwood/docs/pull/432)
amal: Awesome, thanks. One UX ask — could we add a tiny note on the quickstart page that says: "If you use CommonJS, use named requires; if you use ESM or Edge, prefer named imports" so people don't try both patterns blindly.
tara: Good call. I'll put that on the quickstart summary and the troubleshooting section. If anyone else hits a weird edge case, paste the bundler + tsconfig and runtimes here and we'll add it to the docs matrix.
mike: Also logging this as a small DX bug: ticket INF-812 (to track improving package exports + docs).
